Class HttpClient

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net.http.HttpClient
public final class HttpClient extends Object
A minimal HTTP/1.1 client recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno. As with java.net.http.HttpClient, the URL decides how a request travels: an https:// URL goes over TLS (Arduino's WiFiSSLClient and its firmware CA bundle on UNO R4 WiFi, or Linux TLS through Arduino_RouterBridge on UNO Q), an http:// URL over a plain WiFiClient. The port defaults to 443 or 80 and can be given explicitly, as in http://192.168.1.10:8080/led. Requires an active Wifi.begin(String, String) connection or bridge, and a board that supports the scheme: the UNO Q has no plain-HTTP client, for example.

The url (and body for post(String, String, byte[], int, byte[], int, int[]), patch(String, String, byte[], int, byte[], int, int[]) and query(String, String, byte[], int, byte[], int, int[])) must each be a compile-time constant: a string literal, or System.getenv("NAME") of a literal environment-variable name, like Wifi.begin(String, String)'s credentials. The compiler splits the URL into scheme, host, port and path, so nothing is parsed on the board. Call these methods with the literal in hand, never through another method's own String parameter. For request headers or a body that depend on runtime data, use post(String, byte[], int, byte[], int, byte[], int, byte[], int, int[]). For a path that depends on runtime data, use get(String, byte[], int, byte[], int, byte[], int, int[]) with a base URL. Small protocol drivers that also need a runtime method or path can use requestHttps(String, int, String, byte[], int, byte[], int, byte[], int, byte[], int, byte[], int, int[]).

The response body is written into bodyBuffer and the raw response headers into headersBuffer (both caller-owned, fixed-size byte[]), each from index 0 and truncated to its given length. Each method returns the number of body bytes written, or -1 if the connection, TLS setup or certificate validation failed. statusAndHeadersLength (a caller-owned int[2], allocated once outside any loop like the buffers) receives the HTTP status code at index 0 (0 if no status line arrived) and the number of bytes written into headersBuffer at index 1. A request that doesn't complete within the timeout (5 seconds unless setTimeout(int) changed it) is abandoned and returns whatever was captured so far.

  • Method Details

    • setTimeout

      public static void setTimeout(int millis)
      Sets how long every later request waits, in milliseconds: on ESP32 boards (Nano ESP32, M5Stack Cardputer) to connect and then again for the response, elsewhere for the response only, as those boards' WiFi clients take no connect timeout. A value of 0 or less is ignored; the default is 5000. Call it once at startup.

    • setTrustedCertificate

      public static boolean setTrustedCertificate(byte[] certificate, int certificateLength)
      Sets a caller-owned PEM trust anchor for later HTTPS requests. The certificate length excludes the trailing NUL byte, which must remain available in certificate; keep the buffer reachable for as long as requests may use it. Returns false when the selected board cannot install a runtime trust anchor or the arguments are invalid.

    • get

      public static int get(String baseUrl, byte[] pathBuffer, int pathLength, byte[] bodyBuffer, int bodyBufferLength, byte[] headersBuffer, int headersBufferLength, int[] statusAndHeadersLength)
      Sends a GET request to baseUrl (a scheme, host and optional port, with no path of its own) for the path held in the first pathLength ASCII bytes of pathBuffer: for paths that depend on runtime data, such as coordinates read from an earlier response (a runtime String is limited to 31 bytes, far too short for a typical query string). pathLength must be less than 256; a longer or negative length returns -1 without connecting.

    • post

      public static int post(String url, String body, byte[] bodyBuffer, int bodyBufferLength, byte[] headersBuffer, int headersBufferLength, int[] statusAndHeadersLength)

    • post

      public static int post(String url, byte[] requestHeadersBuffer, int requestHeadersLength, byte[] requestBodyBuffer, int requestBodyLength, byte[] bodyBuffer, int bodyBufferLength, byte[] headersBuffer, int headersBufferLength, int[] statusAndHeadersLength)
      Sends a POST request to url with caller-owned request headers and a caller-owned JSON body. The first requestHeadersLength bytes may contain complete HTTP header lines ending in \r\n, without the final blank line; a Content-Type line there replaces the default application/json. The first requestBodyLength bytes form the body. This overload is allocation-free and is intended for small board-side clients whose authentication headers or JSON values are only known at runtime.

    • requestHttps

      public static int requestHttps(String host, int port, String method, byte[] pathBuffer, int pathLength, byte[] requestHeadersBuffer, int requestHeadersLength, byte[] requestBodyBuffer, int requestBodyLength, byte[] bodyBuffer, int bodyBufferLength, byte[] headersBuffer, int headersBufferLength, int[] statusAndHeadersLength)
      Sends an HTTPS request whose host, path, request headers, and optional body are held in caller-owned storage. This lower-level form supports small board-side protocol drivers that need runtime paths or authentication headers without allocating strings. host is a DNS name without https://, a port, or a path. The first pathLength bytes of pathBuffer are the request target. The first requestHeadersLength bytes of requestHeadersBuffer may contain any number of complete HTTP header lines, each ending in \r\n, without the final blank line. A zero length sends no custom headers. A negative requestBodyLength sends no body; otherwise the first that many bytes of requestBodyBuffer are sent as JSON.

      The response contract is the same as get(String, byte[], int, byte[], int, int[]). All storage is caller-owned and the operation is allocation-free. Invalid negative lengths, a path of 256 bytes or more, or a request-header block of 1024 bytes or more return -1 without connecting.

    • requestHttp

      public static int requestHttp(String host, int port, String method, byte[] pathBuffer, int pathLength, byte[] requestHeadersBuffer, int requestHeadersLength, byte[] requestBodyBuffer, int requestBodyLength, byte[] bodyBuffer, int bodyBufferLength, byte[] headersBuffer, int headersBufferLength, int[] statusAndHeadersLength)
      Sends a plain-HTTP request whose host, path, request headers, and optional body are held in caller-owned storage. This is the plain-HTTP counterpart of requestHttps(String, int, String, byte[], int, byte[], int, byte[], int, byte[], int, byte[], int, int[]); it is useful for local devices whose address is entered at runtime. The same length and response-buffer rules apply.
